scope: Original arithmetic audit of vendor public pricing/performance claim, plus bounded external matched-instance benchmark search. No interview conducted and no workloads run by us.
topline: A vendor performance headline becomes materially smaller after including required memory charges. This improves research discipline and creates a precise original interview question; it does not establish an Intel short valuation edge.

oracle_article_inputs.comparison: Intel X12 vs Intel X9 bare metal, not Intel vs AMD
oracle_article_inputs.model: Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct via llama.cpp; AMX-aware quantization described without exact bitwidth/commit

vendor_up_to5_case.status: Illustrative sensitivity, not measured by us

vendor_up_to6_case.status: Illustrative sensitivity, not measured by us

valid_inference: At stated public prices, X12 must deliver about3.55times as many successful tokens per second for equal CPU+memory cost per token on these fixed baremetal shapes. If the reported5–6times throughput is achieved for the same accepted quality/latency, calculated token cost is approximately29–41%lower. No measured dollar/token result can be calculated without absolute valid throughput.
limitations: Vendor up-to throughput was not independently reproduced. The two claimed maxima correspond to different input/output/concurrency settings; do not treat them as a confidence interval.
Model quality, exact quantization, context/prompt data, run count, time-to-first-token, inter-token latency and failure rates were not sufficiently specified for a comparable productioncost test.
Compute list cost includes CPU and allocated memory; excludes boot/storage, data transfer, paid OS/software/support, unused capacity, taxes and contract discounts.
April launch prices match current price schedule, but any private discount or special benchmark billing arrangement is unverified. Seek author clarification before alleging a factual billing error.
Different socket counts, core counts, memory systems and AMX/software paths confound architectural attribution.
No sameOracleX12vsE6Ax matched workload study found. AWS performance data cannot be combined with Oracle prices.
No inference from cloud retail billing to Intel chip ASP, hardware cost, DCAI margin or marketwide workloads.
This is secondary benchmark evidence plus original arithmetic, not an original conducted interview or independently measured benchmark.
candidate_interview_questions: Your July20 X12 article uses120OCPUs and1152GB. The April launch/price list separatesCPU$0.0119 andmemory$0.0114 perGBhour. Does the$1.43/hour example intentionallyexclude memory or use a different billing arrangement? I calculate$14.5608 CPU+memory, versus$4.096 forX9. Which pricing assumption should a reader use?

For each reported5x/6x case, could you share a public run command, llama.cpp commit, exact model/quantization, token counts, repetitions and measured successfultokens/s plus TTFT/ITL? Were accepted output quality and latency constraints equal?
Which workloads failed to achieve the3.55x throughput break-even at these fixed baremetal list configurations, and could right-sized VMs change the ranking?
Would a matched X12/E6Ax comparison use equal advertisedvCPU, equalphysicalcores, equalmonthlybudget or equalSLAcapacity, and why?

external_AWS_measurements.scope: More than120tests, AWS4xlarge families,64GB perinstance, Ubuntu26.04/Linux7.0/GCC15.2
external_AWS_measurements.reported_geo_mean_summary: Graviton5 approximately19%ahead ofIntel;AMDapproximately17%ahead ofGraviton5. Different workloads varied.
external_AWS_measurements.analysis_limit: Primary independent test evidence of purchasable instance economics, not pureper-core architecture, Intelmargin or OCIresults. Raw results403 prevented reproduction; no reprocessed win-count, geometricmean or current AWS-price claim made.

evidence_to_forecast: Use to challenge the claim that AI CPU throughput gains automatically imply customer value or Intel pricing power. It neither identifies a35%matureDCAImargin nor .8capitalproductivity. Those remain scenario assumptions until customer willingness-to-pay and capital requirements are separately evidenced.
